UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis

UPO-06 holds the coding sequence for prhI from Ralstonia solanacearum. That's an ECF sigma factor, and without it, transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system won't happen. PrhR activates the gene. The gene then turns on sigma factor expression by activating the PprhJ promoter. We optimized the sequence for expression in Escherichia coli.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis

UPO-11 gives you the PprhJ promoter region. When a plant cell makes contact, signal transduction through PrhA and PrhR triggers a response, and the ECF sigma factor PrhI activates this promoter. We optimized the sequence for expression in Escherichia coli.

Some of our data representations will be unique to Wikitravel. That sets us apart from other organizations. The real change is the Turtle RDF standard.

Turtle lets us write custom RDF schemas directly. So we use the same wiki techniques to build our own schemas, no separate platform needed.

Subject: What we found for foxl2 in trout

Dear Customer,

Here is what we found on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both transcripts showed up very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a stayed highly restricted in the male. Its diverged paralog foxl2b turned up in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

foxl2b ran the other way: in adult female tissues it stayed highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, foxl2b expression was very strong. That lines up with earlier findings of foxl2b present and foxl2a absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results point to foxl2b as a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your time and interest in our research.

The alitrunk (Fig. 15) is conspicuously swollen and sits well above the propodeal dorsum. Two strong spines arm the propodeum, straight to slightly upcurved. No metanotal groove. The metapleural lobes are triangular and easy to see. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node; its dorsum slopes down posteriorly, leaving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole, the anterior and dorsal surfaces form one convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. From above, the nodes of both the petiole and postpetiole are broader than long. The head dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. Those rugae are irregular and meander a little, usually with a few anastomoses. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, but you will usually find 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and that sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. Every space between the rugae is unsculptured, or at most carries the faintest superficial traces. The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose; the postpetiole runs from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. Fine, acute hairs densely clothe every dorsal surface of the head and body. Color runs from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot back carbon neutrality claims for electricity use beyond a claimant's metered consumption. Most RECs come from projects that would have been financially viable without selling them. [10] Consequently, they lack additionality, an essential attribute. Additionality asks what would have happened under the status quo if the REC had not been purchased or contracted. Many frameworks exist for testing additionality, but the central question stays the same: did the project need REC revenue to survive financially? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs are not the same as genuine emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation based on the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From there, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over uneven bottom.

Using only linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). For the leading-order solution, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while slope square terms remain negligible under the mild-slope assumption. We therefore retained all the modified curvature terms neglected in the MSE, which led to a uniform model.

We built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model predicts the main features of waves over various sea beds, such as sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the uniform model agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

One important result of the FEM model is its use for wave transformation over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

Subject: A Note on the Enduring Legacy of Buraq

Dear Friend,

Once, the world held reality and myth together. Only modern comparative biology drew a line between them. That line never erased the place where a figure like Buraq lives. We still need such figures. They join what we know by measurement to what we know by faith.

Look at how she survives in contemporary culture. She bridges rationalist taxonomies and the leftover power of myth. The Islamic transport industry proves it. There, Buraq, pious and fast, keeps returning as a patron saint. She names airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Why does she travel so easily between aesthetic and linguistic uses? Because she bends. She presides over wings and wheels, and she sells plastic and PVC, heavy metal, and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

Thousands of monsters roam MapleStory. Here's where they live and how to survive them.

The Weak Monsters: The most common foes, and they hang around towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them. Don't worry. Just take the damage.

The Dangerous Ones: The most lethal monsters live deep in dungeons.

The Aggro Mechanic: This one matters. Monsters usually roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. Attack one or cast a debuff on it, though, and you "aggro" it. Now you have its attention, and it will try to hit you back.

Behavioral Pattern: Most enemies attack by running into you over and over again.

The Best Strategy: Against these persistent attackers, the easiest thing to do is hit them repeatedly. Your attacks usually carry enough knockback to keep them in place.

Dodge Tactics: Sometimes you'll need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

Here is what you need to know about early hearing development. Children usually learn to speak within the first few years of life. Hearing impairment can stop a child from learning to speak. It can also stop a child from understanding spoken language.

By the time you notice that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit, communication problems may already have strained the family and held back social skills. If that child belongs to a Deaf community that uses sign language instead of spoken language, these challenges can be reduced (see our article on Deaf Culture).

In many developed countries, newborns get hearing evaluations. The goal is to prevent a deaf child from becoming inadvertently isolated within a hearing family. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy depends on understanding speech. In the vast majority of written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols.

A person who hears well enough to learn to speak and read will keep the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely reads proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that identifying hearing impairment early is key to helping a child with very insensitive hearing learn spoken language effectively. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

I hope this helps you see why early intervention matters. If you have any further questions, please reach out.

Transduction is how physical and chemical signals become neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical inputs are converted by specialized sensory receptors into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system is one example. In the retina, rod and cone cells link the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it causes a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. This molecular shift sets off a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The reduction in this gradient lowers the electrical signals sent to the brain. The result: more light hitting the photoreceptor means fewer electrical impulses, which lets the brain decode the visual world with precision.

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Here are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as the number of voxels multiplied by the volume of the voxel, as long as the compartment has a CT number above zero.

We computed the change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between those same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, which had CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], we classified the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

I look forward to discussing these results with you.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), or just the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It takes in a string of former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

Roughly five million people live here. That is more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Motorways crisscross the area, yet hitchhiking still trips people up, because the minor roads tangle. The motorways that matter are the A1, A2, and A3.

So stick to those three. The smaller roads carry almost no transit traffic, and you will wait a long time on them. Germany treats hitchhikers well. The Ruhr does not. It is the worst stretch of the country for it. Hitching here feels like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul: the cities stand alone, but to you they blur into districts of one enormous city.

We hope this helps you plan a safe, enjoyable trip.

Best regards,

Mobile internet is stretching what a story can be. It brings us electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest step in a decades-long evolution of electronic games, ones that make you an avatar in a gameworld and a co-author alongside the original designers.

Location-aware interfaces let you pull places from the physical world into your gameworld, and push the gameworld back out into those places. Interactive media has never done that before. And beyond giving you a hand in worldmaking, mobile games drop linear narratives and hand storytelling over to the player's experience of place.

The "author-player" worldmaking idea is old. Mobile games push it past what traditional video games allow. They carry worldmaking off the screen and into the physical world, where location-aware interfaces grab your sensory experience of real places and turn it into a storytelling tool.

In our essay, we theorize what storytelling can do in mobile games, and we describe our own attempt to use it while designing and building our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
